text.content:
The Storytelling for Elders chapter is mostly Storyteller-facing craft advice on scale, scope, theme, character creation and plot construction for an all-elder chronicle, and on integrating one or two elders into an already-running chronicle. That material is prose guidance rather than game data and isn't reproduced here. Two pieces of it are concrete enough to use directly at the table: a named list of ready-made elder plot hooks, and a short list of warning signs that a chronicle's elder power level has gotten out of hand. Both are collected below for Storyteller reference.

Elder Plot Hooks

Ready-made reasons to drop a new elder character into an ongoing chronicle:

  • Rivals: Introduce two or more elders with backgrounds that intersect, giving them built-in reason to view each other as competitors.
  • Clan Matters: The elder arrives as a representative of her clan, bearing a message or instructions for clanmates already in the city, and is ordered to remain and assist.
  • Traitor: The elder is fleeing those she betrayed — a renegade Tremere hiding from the Council of Seven, or a Brujah anarch who abandoned her pack.
  • Archons: The elders are a coterie of archons serving a Justicar, arriving in secret to pose as ordinary Kindred while investigating the city's other characters for Tradition violations.
  • Infiltrator: The elder is a Sabbat pack leader covertly recruiting new members from the city's anarchs and disgruntled Kindred.
  • Prince's Lackey: The elder is sent by her sire as a favor to the prince, to serve as a new functionary while learning the nuances of ruling a city.
  • Methuselah Agent: The elder is a spy for an ancient vampire recently risen from torpor, tasked with reporting on how the world and the local Kindred have changed.
  • Prince: The elder arrives to claim domain or usurp a weak or absent prince, galvanizing the city's Kindred for or against her. Works best in a city currently without a strong prince.

Before introducing any of these, consider how the incoming elder will alter existing plot threads and subplots, whether her Disciplines or Abilities trivialize an ongoing challenge (e.g., easily finding a hidden Setite temple), and how neonates and ancillae are likely to react to and gravitate toward her.

Troubleshooting: Elder Power Escalating Out of Control

Warning signs that the elder power level in a chronicle has gotten away from the Storyteller:

  • Elders turn every minor disagreement into a lethal showdown.
  • Sessions frequently degenerate into prolonged mob combats while noncombatant players are bored.
  • Players act irresponsibly and disregard the Masquerade, relying on elder power to bail them out of foolhardy actions; key story elements are ignored in favor of Physical Challenges and combat.
  • Other players ask the Storyteller to intervene against a specific disruptive player.
  • Characters die with alarming frequency at the hands of elders.

Do not respond by escalating power further — mutually-assured-destruction does not deter this behavior and only increases disruption. Instead: hold a post-mortem discussion with the troupe, talk privately with the players most involved, and consider whether the group needs to restart with less powerful characters, whether a single disruptive player needs a private conversation about modifying his behavior, or whether some plot elements need retooling so elders can no longer bulldoze them by main force. If a problem player refuses to change after a genuine attempt at correction, ask him not to return.
